1.a: Moses (the Lord Jesus speaks of the books of Moses: Luke 24:44; John 5:46).
1.w: During Israel's forty years in the wilderness, after the Exodus.
1.th: The beginning: creation, the fall of man, the flood, and God's covenant promise to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, through whose seed all nations would be blessed.
o: The flood, and the nations after it

2.w: In the wilderness, after the Exodus.
2.th: The Lord redeems His people out of bondage in Egypt, gives them His law at Sinai, and comes to dwell among them in the tabernacle.
o: Bondage in Egypt and the call of Moses
The golden calf, and the covenant renewed
The tabernacle built and filled with the glory of the Lord

3.th: How a sinful people may draw near to a holy God: sacrifice, priesthood and holy living. "Ye shall be holy: for I the LORD your God am holy."
o: A holy people: laws for holy living, feasts and vows

4.th: Israel numbered and led through the wilderness; the unbelief at Kadesh and forty years of wandering; God's faithfulness to a new generation.
o: From Sinai to Moab: complaining and unbelief
The new generation prepares to enter the land

5.a: Moses (Deuteronomy 31:9, 24); the account of his death (chapter 34) was added after him.
5.w: On the plains of Moab, at the end of the forty years.
5.to: The new generation about to enter Canaan.
5.th: Moses repeats the law and calls Israel to love the Lord with all their heart and to obey Him in the land He was giving them.
o: Blessings and curses; the choice set before Israel
Moses' last words, song and blessing, and his death

6.a: Joshua (Joshua 24:26), with later additions such as the account of his death.
6.th: The Lord keeps His promise: Israel crosses the Jordan, conquers the land and divides it among the tribes.

7.a: Not named in Scripture; traditionally Samuel.
7.w: In the early days of the kingdom (see 17:6, "In those days there was no king in Israel").
7.th: Again and again Israel turns from the Lord, is oppressed, cries out, and is delivered by judges He raises up.
o: Israel's failure to finish the conquest

8.a: Not named in Scripture; traditionally Samuel.
8.w: Set "in the days when the judges ruled" (1:1); written after David was born (4:22).
8.th: The faithfulness of Ruth and the kindness of Boaz, a kinsman-redeemer; God provides a line leading to David, and so to Christ.
o: Naomi and Ruth return to Bethlehem
Ruth in the field of Boaz
Boaz redeems; the line of David

9.a: Not named; Samuel, Nathan and Gad wrote the acts of David (1 Chronicles 29:29).
9.w: In the time of the kings.
9.th: Israel moves from the judges to a king: Samuel, the rejected king Saul, and the rise of David, the man after God's own heart.
o: David anointed, and Saul's pursuit of him

10.w: In the time of the kings.
10.th: The reign of David: his triumphs, God's covenant to establish his throne for ever, his sin with Bathsheba and its bitter fruit.
o: David's triumphs and God's covenant with him
Troubles in David's house: Absalom's rebellion

11.a: Not named in Scripture; traditionally Jeremiah.
11.w: During or after the exile (2 Kings ends with the exile).
11.th: Solomon's glory and the temple; the kingdom divided; the ministry of Elijah. Faithfulness to the Lord brings blessing, idolatry brings ruin.

12.a: Not named in Scripture; traditionally Jeremiah.
12.th: The ministry of Elisha, and the decline of both kingdoms until Israel is carried to Assyria and Judah to Babylon.
o: Israel and Judah to the fall of Samaria
Judah alone, to the exile in Babylon

13.a: Not named in Scripture; traditionally Ezra.
13.to: The Jews who returned from Babylon.
13.th: The line of God's people from Adam, and the reign of David, with special care for the ark, the priesthood and the worship of God.

14.a: Not named in Scripture; traditionally Ezra.
14.to: The Jews who returned from Babylon.
14.th: The house of David from Solomon to the exile, told with an eye on the temple; seeking the Lord brings revival.
o: The kings of Judah, to the exile and Cyrus's decree

15.a: Ezra the scribe (he speaks in the first person in chapters 7 to 9).
15.th: The Lord stirs up Cyrus; the people return, rebuild the temple, and are taught and reformed by the law of God.
o: The first return and the temple rebuilt

16.a: Nehemiah: "The words of Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah" (1:1).
16.w: In the days of Artaxerxes king of Persia (2:1).
16.th: The walls of Jerusalem rebuilt in the face of opposition, and the people renewed in covenant with God.
o: The law read and the covenant renewed
The city settled and further reforms

17.a: Not named in Scripture; traditionally Mordecai.
17.w: In the days of Ahasuerus king of Persia (1:1).
17.th: Though His name is not mentioned, God preserves His people through Esther and Mordecai; the feast of Purim.

18.w: The events are set in the days of the patriarchs.
18.th: A righteous man suffers; his friends' answers fail; the Lord speaks out of the whirlwind, and Job is humbled and restored.

19.a: David and others, as the titles show: Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Moses, Heman and Ethan; many are not named.
19.w: Over many centuries, from Moses to after the exile.
19.th: The prayer and praise book of God's people, in every season of life; many psalms speak of Christ.

20.a: Chiefly Solomon (1:1; 10:1; 25:1); also Agur (30:1) and king Lemuel (31:1).
20.w: In the days of Solomon, some collected under Hezekiah (25:1).
20.th: Wise and godly living. "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge."
o: The words of Agur and Lemuel; the virtuous woman

21.a: "The Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem" (1:1); traditionally Solomon.
21.w: In the days of the kings.
21.th: Life "under the sun" without God is vanity; the end of the matter: "Fear God, and keep his commandments."

22.th: A song of love between the bridegroom and his bride, long read as a picture of the love between the Lord and His people.
o: Love that many waters cannot quench

23.a: Isaiah the son of Amoz (1:1); the Lord Jesus and the apostles quote him by name (e.g. John 12:38-41).
23.w: In the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah (1:1).
23.th: The Holy One of Israel judges sin and promises salvation through His Servant, the Messiah, who would be wounded for our transgressions.
o: Comfort: the Lord alone is God

24.a: Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah (1:1), with Baruch as his scribe (36:4).
24.w: From the thirteenth year of Josiah to the captivity of Jerusalem (1:2-3).
24.th: The weeping prophet calls Judah to repent before Babylon comes, and foretells a new covenant written on the heart.
o: Jeremiah's sufferings, and the new covenant

25.a: Not named in Scripture; traditionally Jeremiah.
25.th: Mourning over ruined Jerusalem, and hope in the Lord's mercies, which are new every morning.
o: The siege remembered; a prayer for restoration

26.a: Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi (1:3).
26.w: Among the captives by the river Chebar in Babylon (1:1-3).
26.th: The glory of the Lord departs from the temple because of sin; judgment on Jerusalem and the nations; a new heart, dry bones living, and a new temple.
o: The vision of the new temple

27.a: Daniel (he speaks in the first person in chapters 7 to 12; the Lord Jesus names him, Matthew 24:15).
27.w: In Babylon, from Nebuchadnezzar to Cyrus (1:1, 21).
27.th: God rules over the kingdoms of men; faithfulness in a foreign land; visions of the kingdoms to come and the everlasting kingdom of God.
o: Daniel and his friends in Babylon

28.w: In the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and Jeroboam king of Israel (1:1).
28.th: Hosea's marriage to an unfaithful wife pictures Israel's unfaithfulness and the Lord's unfailing love.
o: The Lord's case against Israel, and His love

29.th: A plague of locusts warns of the great day of the Lord; a call to repent, and the promise of the Spirit poured out (Acts 2:16).
o: The day of the Lord, and the Spirit promised

30.w: In the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel (1:1).
30.th: Judgment on the nations and on Israel for injustice and empty religion; "let judgment run down as waters."

31.w: Not stated; after Edom rejoiced over Jerusalem's fall (verses 11-14).
31.th: Edom's pride and violence against his brother Jacob will be judged; the kingdom shall be the Lord's.
o: The judgment of Edom and the deliverance of Zion

32.a: Not named; the book is about Jonah the son of Amittai (1:1; 2 Kings 14:25).
32.w: In the time of the kings of Israel.
32.th: The Lord's mercy reaches even to Nineveh; Jonah's three days in the fish are a sign of Christ's resurrection (Matthew 12:40).

33.w: In the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah (1:1).
33.th: Judgment for sin, and hope in the ruler to be born in Bethlehem; what the Lord requires.
o: The coming kingdom and the ruler from Bethlehem
The Lord's case, and His mercy

34.th: The fall of Nineveh: the Lord is slow to anger but will not acquit the wicked; a stronghold for those who trust Him.

35.w: Not stated; as the Chaldeans were rising (1:6).
35.th: The prophet asks why evil goes unpunished; the Lord answers, and the prophet learns that "the just shall live by his faith."
o: Habakkuk's questions and the Lord's answers

36.a: Zephaniah, of the line of Hizkiah (1:1).
36.w: In the days of Josiah king of Judah (1:1).
36.th: The great day of the Lord is near; judgment on Judah and the nations, then joy: the Lord will rejoice over His people with singing.
o: The day of the Lord on Judah

37.w: In the second year of Darius (1:1), after the return from exile.
37.to: Zerubbabel, Joshua and the returned Jews.
37.th: Consider your ways: put the Lord's house first; the glory of the latter house.

38.w: In the second year of Darius (1:1).
38.th: Visions of encouragement to rebuild, and prophecies of the coming King, lowly and riding upon an ass.
o: The coming King and His kingdom

39.w: After the return, when the temple stood again.
39.th: The Lord's love questioned and His people's worship careless; the messenger who would prepare the way of the Lord.
o: The Lord's case against priests and people
The messenger, and the day of the Lord

40.a: Matthew the apostle, the publican (Matthew 9:9; 10:3), by early testimony.
40.w: Not stated; before the fall of Jerusalem is the usual view.
40.th: Jesus is the Christ, the Son of David, the King foretold by the prophets.
o: The birth and preparation of the King
Toward Jerusalem, and teaching on the last things
The death and resurrection of the King

41.a: John Mark (Acts 12:12), by early testimony companion of Peter.
41.th: Jesus, the Son of God, the Servant who came not to be ministered unto but to minister and give His life a ransom.
o: The Servant at work in Galilee

42.a: Luke, "the beloved physician" (Colossians 4:14), who also wrote Acts (Acts 1:1).
42.th: An orderly account of Jesus, the Son of man, who came to seek and to save that which was lost.

43.a: John the apostle, "the disciple whom Jesus loved" (21:20, 24).
43.th: That ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing ye might have life through His name.
o: With His disciples: the upper room

44.w: Not stated; the book ends with Paul in Rome.
44.th: The risen Lord, by His Spirit, spreads the gospel "in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth."

45.th: The gospel is the power of God unto salvation: all have sinned, and are justified freely by grace through faith in Christ.
o: Life in Christ and in the Spirit

46.to: The church of God at Corinth (1:2).
46.th: Correcting divisions and disorders in the church; the way of love; the resurrection of the dead.

47.th: Paul's ministry: comfort in trouble, the new covenant, generous giving, and God's strength made perfect in weakness.

48.th: Justified by faith, not by the works of the law; stand fast in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free.
o: Faith, not the works of the law
Liberty and the life of the Spirit

49.a: Paul (1:1), as "the prisoner of the Lord" (4:1).
49.th: Every spiritual blessing in Christ; saved by grace through faith; one body; walking worthy of the calling.
o: Walking worthy: in the church, the home and the battle

50.th: Joy in the Lord in every circumstance; the mind of Christ, who humbled Himself.

51.th: Christ is preeminent, the image of the invisible God, and complete in Him we need nothing more.

52.th: Thanks for their faith; holy living; the Lord's coming and the hope of believers who have died.
o: Holy living and the Lord's coming

53.th: Comfort in persecution; the day of the Lord is not yet come; work quietly and be not weary in well doing.
o: The man of sin, and the day of the Lord

54.to: Timothy, his "own son in the faith" (1:2).
54.th: Order in the church: sound doctrine, prayer, the qualifications of overseers and deacons, and godliness with contentment.
o: Prayer, and the leaders of the church
A good minister of Jesus Christ

55.w: From prison, near the end of his life (1:8; 4:6).
55.th: Paul's last letter: be strong, endure hardness, hold fast the Scriptures given by inspiration of God, and preach the word.
o: Continue in the Scriptures; preach the word

56.th: Ordaining elders, sound doctrine, and good works that adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour.
o: Good works, and the kindness of God

57.th: Paul asks Philemon to receive back Onesimus, his runaway servant, now a brother beloved in Christ.

58.a: Not named in Scripture; many have held it to be Paul's.
58.w: Before the destruction of the temple, while sacrifices were still offered (10:11).
58.th: Christ is better: better than the angels, Moses and the priesthood; His one sacrifice for sins for ever; hold fast in faith.
o: Christ above Moses; a rest for the people of God
Christ our great high priest and His one sacrifice
Run the race, looking unto Jesus

59.a: James, "a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ" (1:1); by early testimony the Lord's brother (Galatians 1:19).
59.th: True faith shows itself in works: patience in trials, a tamed tongue, and care for the poor.
o: Trials, and doers of the word
The tongue, and wisdom from above

60.a: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ (1:1), by Silvanus (5:12).
60.to: The strangers scattered in Asia Minor (1:1).
60.th: A living hope in suffering: be holy, follow Christ's example, and cast all your care upon Him.
o: A living hope and a holy people

61.w: Near the end of his life (1:14).
61.to: Those who have obtained like precious faith (1:1).
61.th: Grow in grace; Scripture is sure; beware false teachers; the day of the Lord will come.
o: Grow in grace; the sure word

62.a: Not named in the letter; by early testimony John the apostle, an eyewitness (1:1).
62.th: God is light and God is love; walk in the light, love one another, and know that ye have eternal life.

63.a: "The elder" (verse 1); by early testimony John the apostle.
63.th: Walk in truth and love; do not receive those who deny that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh.

64.a: "The elder" (verse 1); by early testimony John the apostle.
64.th: Commendation for Gaius's hospitality to the brethren; a warning about Diotrephes.

65.th: Earnestly contend for the faith once delivered unto the saints; God is able to keep you from falling.

66.th: The revelation of Jesus Christ: His letters to the churches, the judgments to come, the triumph of the Lamb, and a new heaven and a new earth.
o: The triumph of Christ, and all things new
